extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and practitioners (attorneys, agents) prosecuting applications before the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedures for filing and formatting amendments, affidavits/declarations, interviews, replies, extensions, and abandonment issues during patent prosecution before the USPTO (including post-final and transitional procedures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments and affidavits after final action and prior to appeal (§ 1.116)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment after final action must comply with § 1.114 or this section. After a final rejection or other final action ... but before or on the same date of filing an appeal: (1) an amendment may be made canceling claims or complying with any requirement of form expressly set forth in a previous Office action; (2) an amendment presenting rejected claims in better form for consideration on appeal may be admitted; or (3) an amendment touching the merits ... may be admitted upon a showing of good and sufficient reasons why the amendment is necessary and was not earlier presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admission or refusal to admit any amendment after final action does not relieve the application from being subject to appeal or save it from abandonment. Special restrictions apply in inter partes reexamination (no substantive amendments after right of appeal except as provided in specified sections). Affidavits or other evidence after final action may be admitted upon a showing of good and sufficient reasons; inter partes reexamination has additional limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner of amending the specification (§ 1.121(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to the specification, other than the claims, must be made by adding, deleting, or replacing a paragraph; by replacing a section; or by providing a substitute specification, in the manner specified in this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions must unambiguously identify location(s). Replacement or added text must show changes relative to the prior version: added subject matter underlined; deleted matter shown by strike-through (or double brackets for five or fewer characters); deleted subject matter may be indicated within double brackets if strike-through not easily perceived. Full text of replacement paragraphs or added paragraphs required. Previously deleted paragraph/section may be reinstated only by subsequent amendment adding it back. Once a paragraph/section is amended in a first amendment document, it must not be represented in a subsequent amendment document unless amended again or a substitute specification is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment by replacement section or substitute specification (§ 1.121(b)(2)-(3); § 1.125)
rubrics_metrics.description: If sections contain headings, amendments may be made by deleting and replacing a section with a replacement section showing all changes. The specification may also be amended by submitting an instruction to replace the specification and a substitute specification in compliance with §§ 1.125(b) and (c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A substitute specification may be required if papers are illegible or too changed to consider; subject to § 1.312, a substitute (excluding claims) may be filed up to payment of the issue fee if accompanied by a statement that it includes no new matter. Substitute specifications must include markings showing all changes relative to the immediate prior version and be accompanied by a clean version. Substitute specifications are not permitted in reissue applications or reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim amendment requirements and claim listing (§ 1.121(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to a claim must be made by rewriting the entire claim with all changes indicated, except when the claim is being canceled. Each amendment document that changes, cancels, or adds claims must include a complete listing of all claims ever presented, including text of all pending and withdrawn claims; the claim listing will replace all prior versions of the claims in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Status of every claim must be indicated using identifiers: (Original), (Currently amended), (Canceled), (Withdrawn), (Previously presented), (New), (Not entered). Claims in listing presented in ascending numerical order. All claims currently amended must show markings (underlining for added, strike-through/double brackets for deleted). Claims not currently amended must be presented in clean version (no markings). Cancellation effected by instruction to cancel particular claim number; reinstatement of a previously canceled claim only by adding it as a 'new' claim with a new claim number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings amendment requirements (§ 1.121(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes to application drawings must be in compliance with § 1.84 (and other sections for international design applications) and submitted on a replacement sheet labeled 'Replacement Sheet' as an attachment to the amendment document. Any replacement sheet must include all figures that appeared on the immediate prior version of the sheet, even if only one figure is amended. New sheets with additional figures must be labeled 'New Sheet.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All changes to drawings must be explained in detail in the drawing amendment or remarks section of the amendment paper. A marked-up copy of amended drawing figures (annotated sheet) may be included and must be clearly labeled 'Annotated Sheet'; such annotated sheets must be presented in the amendment or remarks section and must be provided when required by the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure consistency and prohibition on new matter (§ 1.121(e)-(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure must be amended, when required by the Office, to correct inaccuracies and to secure substantial correspondence between the claims, the remainder of the specification, and the drawings. No amendment may introduce new matter into the disclosure of an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office may require amendments to ensure consistency. Introducing any new matter is prohibited and will not be permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception for examiner's amendments (§ 1.121(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes to the specification, including the claims, made by the Office in an examiner's amendment may be made by specific instructions to insert or delete subject matter set forth in the examiner's amendment by identifying the precise point in the specification or the claim(s) where the insertion or deletion is to be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance with paragraphs (b)(1), (b)(2), or (c) of this section is not required for examiner's amendments executed by such specific instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment document organization (§ 1.121(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each section of an amendment document (e.g., amendment to the claims, amendment to the specification, replacement drawings, and remarks) must begin on a separate sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure separate sheets for different amendment sections; claim listing must commence on a separate sheet and sheets containing claim text shall not contain other parts of the amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering and preservation of claim numbers (§ 1.126)
rubrics_metrics.description: The original numbering of the claims must be preserved throughout the prosecution. When claims are canceled the remaining claims must not be renumbered. When claims are added, they shall be numbered consecutively beginning with the number next following the highest numbered claim previously presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the application is ready for allowance, the examiner, if necessary, will renumber the claims consecutively in the order they appear or in an order requested by applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional limited examination after final rejection (§ 1.129(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant in an application (other than reissue or design) pending at least two years as of June 8, 1995 is entitled to have a first submission entered and considered on the merits after final rejection if the first submission and the fee in § 1.17(r) are filed prior to filing an appeal brief and prior to abandonment; the finality of the final rejection is automatically withdrawn upon timely filing of the submission and payment of the fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant entitled to a second submission under similar conditions; any submission filed after the fee has been paid twice will be treated under § 1.116. 'Submission' includes IDS, amendment to written description/claims/drawings, and new substantive argument or evidence in support of patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional restriction practice for long-pending applications (§ 1.129(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: In an application pending at least three years as of June 8, 1995, no requirement for restriction or for filing divisional applications shall be made or maintained after June 8, 1995, except where (i) the requirement was first made prior to April 8, 1995 in the application or earlier application; (ii) examiner has not made a restriction requirement prior to April 8, 1995 due to actions by applicant; or (iii) required fee for examination of each additional invention was not paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application contains more than one independent and distinct invention and a restriction cannot be made under this paragraph, the applicant will be notified and given time to elect invention(s) to be searched and examined and to pay fees, or to file a petition traversing the requirement. Additional inventions for which the required fee has not been paid will be withdrawn from consideration and may be pursued by filing a divisional application under 35 U.S.C. 121.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit or declaration of attribution or prior public disclosure under the AIA (§ 1.130)
rubrics_metrics.description: When any claim is rejected, the applicant or patent owner may submit an affidavit or declaration to disqualify a disclosure as prior art by establishing that the disclosure was made by the inventor or joint inventor, or the subject matter was obtained from the inventor or joint inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For prior public disclosure affidavits: identify the subject matter and provide the date of public disclosure; if printed publication, include copy; if not printed, describe with sufficient detail and particularity to determine what was disclosed. Not available if the disclosure is more than one year before the effective filing date. If the rejection is based on a U.S. patent/application publication naming another inventor and derivation is claimed, a derivation petition may be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit or declaration of prior invention; disqualification of commonly owned art (§ 1.131)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant or owner may submit an oath or declaration to establish invention prior to the effective date of the reference or to disqualify a commonly owned patent or published application as prior art under certain conditions (including ownership and non-patentably-distinct inventions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Showing must be sufficient in character and weight to establish reduction to practice prior to the reference, or conception prior to the reference coupled with due diligence to reduction to practice or filing. Original exhibits of drawings or records (or explained absence) must accompany the affidavit/declaration. Prior invention rules have geographic and date limits (U.S., NAFTA, WTO members; limited effective dates). To disqualify commonly owned art under § 103 a terminal disclaimer and an oath/declaration of common ownership and prior inventor may be required. Prior invention is not available when rejection is based on interfering subject matter or statutory bar in certain situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits or declarations traversing rejections or objections (§ 1.132)
rubrics_metrics.description: When any claim is rejected or objected to, any evidence submitted to traverse the rejection or objection on a basis not otherwise provided for must be by way of an oath or declaration under this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence submitted to traverse must take the form of the specified affidavit/declaration; normal documentary submissions without the required oath/declaration will not suffice for traversing on novel bases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews with examiners (§ 1.133)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews with examiners concerning applications and other matters pending before the Office must be conducted on Office premises and within Office hours as designated by the respective examiners. An interview for the discussion of the patentability of a pending application will not occur before the first Office action, unless the application is a continuing or substitute application or the examiner determines that such an interview would advance prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner may require an interview be scheduled in advance. Where reconsideration is requested in view of an interview, a complete written statement of the reasons presented at the interview must be filed. An interview does not remove the necessity for reply to Office actions as specified in §§ 1.111 and 1.135.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time period for reply to an Office action (§ 1.134)
rubrics_metrics.description: An Office action will notify the applicant of any non-statutory or shortened statutory time period set for reply to an Office action. Unless the applicant is notified in writing that a reply is required in less than six months, a maximum period of six months is allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default maximum reply period is six months unless the Office specifies a shorter time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment for failure to reply within time period (§ 1.135)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant fails to reply within the time period provided under §§ 1.134 and 1.136, the application will become abandoned unless an Office action indicates otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To save from abandonment prosecution must include a complete and proper reply as the condition of the application may require. Admission or refusal to admit amendments after final rejection or any amendment not responsive to the last action will not save the application from abandonment. If the reply is a bona fide attempt to advance the application but inadvertently omits some matter, applicant may be given a new time period for reply to supply the omission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time to reply (§ 1.136)
rubrics_metrics.description: If required to reply within a nonstatutory or shortened statutory time period, applicant may extend the time up to the earlier of the statutory maximum or five months after the time period set for reply, if a petition for extension and the prescribed fee are filed, unless exceptions apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions where extension under paragraph (a) not available include: applicant notified otherwise in an Office action; the reply is a reply brief under § 41.41; the reply is a request for oral hearing under § 41.47(a); the reply is to a PTAB decision under § 41.50/41.52 or § 90.3; or the application is in a contested case or derivation proceeding. The date the petition and fee are filed determines the period of extension and amount of fee. A reply must be filed prior to expiration of the extension period to avoid abandonment, and an applicant may not reply later than the maximum statutory period nor be granted an extension when paragraph (a) provisions are available.
